questions.answer: Yes, I like to stay [[informed]], mostly through news apps and a bit of online reading. I try not to overdo it, though, because too much news can be draining. A quick daily catch-up is usually enough.

questions.q: What kind of news are you most interested in?
questions.answer: Mostly education and international news, since both relate to my job. Changes to student visa rules abroad, for example, directly affect the students I advise, so I [[keep a close eye]] on them.

questions.q: How do you usually get your news?
questions.answer: Almost entirely online, through my phone. It's quick and I can check headlines whenever I have a spare moment. I rarely watch the news on television any more, which feels [[outdated]] to me now.

questions.q: Did your family watch the news together when you were young?
questions.answer: Every evening, yes. My father [[religiously]] watched the eight o'clock news, and we all had to stay quiet until it finished. As a child I found it boring, but now I realise how much I picked up just by listening.

questions.q: Do you trust the news you read online?
questions.answer: Not everything, no. There's a lot of misleading content online, especially on social media, so I try to [[cross-check]] stories with reliable sources before believing them. I think media literacy should really be taught in schools now.
